source.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry

accepted.question_text: Given only random samples from an unknown polytope in R^n, can the polytope be learned efficiently? More specifically, although the volume of a polytope can be computed efficiently when one has membership-oracle access, is there a polynomial-time procedure that reconstructs or approximately learns the polytope from random sample points alone?
accepted.context_brief: Learning a polytope from random samples

evidence.quote: For example, while we know how to efficiently compute the volume of a polytope, learning one efficiently from random samples is an open problem.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every convex body K in R^n admits an ellipsoid E with the following approximate sandwiching property: at least half the volume of E lies inside K, and at least half the volume of K lies inside the dilated ellipsoid C log n · E?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5. There exists a constant C such that for any convex body K in R^n, there exists an ellipsoid E that satisfies approximate sandwiching: vol(E ∩ K) ≥ 1/2 vol(E); vol(K ∩ C log nE) ≥ 1/2 vol(K).

accepted.question_text: If X is drawn from an isotropic logconcave density f on R^n, must the variance of the squared Euclidean norm ||X||^2 always be at most Cn for some absolute constant C? Equivalently, must isotropic logconcave measures have most of their mass concentrated in a thin Euclidean shell of constant-width scale after normalization?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 12 (Thin shell). For X drawn from a logconcave isotropic density f in R^n, Var_f (||X||^2) ≤ Cn

accepted.question_text: For every logconcave density f on R^n with covariance matrix A_f, is the isoperimetric coefficient Φ_f always bounded below by c / sqrt(λ_1(A_f)) for some absolute constant c, where λ_1(A_f) is the largest eigenvalue of A_f?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 19 (KLS). Let f be a logconcave density in R^n. There is an absolute constant c such that Φ_f ≥ c / sqrt(λ_1(A_f)).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every isotropic logconcave density f on R^n satisfies f(0) ≤ C^n? In the equivalent convex-body form highlighted in the paper, does every isotropic convex body in R^n have volume at least c^n for some absolute constant c?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 21 (Slicing). There exists a constant C, such that for an isotropic logconcave density f in R^n, f(0) ≤ C^n.

accepted.question_text: Let f be a logconcave density on R^n, and let P be any partition of R^n into convex parts. Is there an absolute constant C such that the sum over parts P of σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) is always at most Cσ_f^2, where σ_f^2 is the largest variance of f in any direction and σ_f(P)^2 is the largest directional variance of the restriction of f to the part P?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 26. Let f be a logconcave density function and P be any partition of R^n such that each part is convex. Then there exists a constant C such that Σ_P σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) ≤ Cσ_f^2 where σ_f^2 is the largest variance of f along any direction and σ_f(P)^2 is the largest variance of f restricted to the set P.

accepted.question_text: Can an intersection of two halfspaces be PAC-learned in polynomial time? More generally, is there a polynomial-time PAC-learning algorithm for this class that avoids the current gap between efficiently learning a single halfspace and the still-open two-halfspace case?

evidence.quote: It is a major open problem to PAC-learn an intersection of two halfspaces.

accepted.question_text: Is there a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming, meaning an algorithm whose running time can be bounded polynomially in the dimension and combinatorial input size without dependence on numerical accuracy parameters arising from repeated rescaling?

evidence.quote: In principle, such a dependence can be avoided for linear programming and it is a major open problem to find a strongly polynomial algorithm for solving linear programs.

accepted.question_text: For either hit-and-run or the ball walk on a convex body, is there a single deterministic starting point that is as effective as a warm start for mixing? For example, if one starts the walk at the centroid, does it converge at the same asymptotic rate as when started from a random warm-start distribution?

evidence.quote: One open problem for both hit-and-run and the ball walk is to find a single starting point that is as good a start as a warm start. E.g., does one of these walks started at the centroid converge at the same rate as starting from a random point?

accepted.question_text: Can the reflection walk based on a separation oracle be analyzed sharply enough to show that it needs only O*(nD) oracle calls for a convex body of diameter D, or even O*(n) oracle calls for isotropic bodies?

evidence.quote: It is possible that for this process, the number of oracle calls (not the number of Markov chain steps) is only O*(nD) rather than O*(n^2D^2), and even O*(n) for isotropic bodies. It is a very interesting open problem to analyze the reflection walk.

accepted.question_text: Which broader classes of distributions or geometric spaces admit efficient random-walk sampling algorithms? In particular, can one give a sufficient condition, phrased in terms of isoperimetry together with a suitable local regularity property of the target density, that guarantees efficient sampling, and can such a framework cover manifolds of nonnegative curvature?

evidence.quote: Our next open problem is to understand classes of distributions that can be efficiently sampled by random walks. ... Can one provide a sufficient condition that depends on isoperimetry and some local property of the density to be sampled? More concretely, for what manifolds with nonnegative curvature (for which isoperimetry is known) can an efficient sampling process be defined?

accepted.question_text: Can one sample lattice points in a convex body under substantially weaker geometric assumptions than the currently known large-inscribed-ball condition? For example, is efficient sampling possible for lattice points of a near-isotropic convex body, or for a body that contains at least half of a ball of radius O(sqrt(n))?
accepted.context_brief: Sampling lattice points in convex bodies

evidence.quote: Can this condition be improved substantially? E.g., can one sample lattice points of a near-isotropic convex body? Or lattice points of a body that contains at least half of a ball of radius O(√n)?

accepted.question_text: Is there a substantially faster random-walk-based optimization method for logconcave optimization whose analysis tracks direct progress toward the optimum, rather than relying on the intermediate task of producing nearly random samples from changing distributions?

evidence.quote: It is conceivable that a random walk type method can be substantially faster if its goal is optimization and its analysis directly measures progress on some distance function, rather than relying on the intermediate step of producing a random sample.

accepted.question_text: Can the volume of a polytope with a bounded number of facets be computed efficiently from a random sample drawn from the polytope, without using an annealing sequence of changing sampling distributions?
accepted.context_brief: Volume from random samples of a polytope

evidence.quote: On the other hand, it remains open to efficiently compute the volume from a random sample for polytopes with a bounded number of facets.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a polytope in R^n with m facets. Is there an algorithm with complexity polynomial in m, n, and 1/ε that learns P from either uniform random points sampled from P or from samples drawn from a Gaussian distribution restricted as described in the source?
accepted.context_brief: Learning a polytope with m facets

evidence.quote: Thus an interesting open problem is to learn a polytope in R^n with m facets given either uniform random points from it or from a Gaussian. It is conceivable that the complexity is poly(m, n, 1/ε).
